newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says blood safety proposals due this year.
newsitem.headline: EU says blood safety proposals due this year.

text.p: The European Commission said on Thursday it will present proposals this year to ensure the safety of blood and plasma used in transfusions, even though the European Union has no binding powers in this area.

The Commission was reacting to a call on Wednesday from Dutch Health Minister Els Borst for EU health ministers to press ahead without waiting for a proposal and agree in June on a common approach to guaranteeing blood safety.
"The Commission regrets the impression which seems to have been given by the Dutch Presidency concerning the role and efforts of the Commission in this important field," it said in a statement.
"The Commission also regrets that information and data that it needs for work in this area from some Member States, including the Netherlands, are not always forthcoming," it added.
The Commission added that it had laid down strict requirements to ensure the safety and quality of medicinal products coming from blood and plasma over which the EU has binding powers.

It noted that political agreement on the importance of blood safety and self-sufficiency had already been reflected in resolutions from the EU Council of Ministers and the European Parliament following a Commission report in December 1994.

Dutch officials said on Wednesday that 1989 EU legislation on the free movement of blood products showed that EU powers existed and that blood safety was too important an issue to wait for the Commission to act.
